engine_name: Ollama (ollama/ollama), versions ~0.20.x (current as of mid-2026). Wraps a bundled/forked llama.cpp engine; serves Gemma 4 via its model library tags (gemma4:31b, gemma4:31b-it-q4_K_M, gemma4:31b-nvfp4, gemma4:31b-coding-mtp-bf16).
cuda_128_compatible: Yes. The official Ollama Linux installer ships pre-built CUDA runners targeting CUDA 12.x including 12.8; no source compilation is needed for a host-native install. The single install script (curl https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh) downloads ollama-linux-amd64.tar.zst, installs to /usr/local, creates an 'ollama' user (added to render/video groups), and creates+enables a systemd service bound to 127.0.0.1:11434. On the target A6000 (sm_86, driver 570.195, CUDA 12.8) this is a fully supported, mature configuration — A6000/Ampere has been supported for years and is far less risky than the newer Blackwell (sm_120) cards, which had CUDA-runner/CC-12.0 detection problems (Issue #13163, PR #9350). Note: nvidia-smi must show driver 570.x+ / CUDA 12.8; on a driver/CUDA mismatch Ollama silently falls back to CPU without an error. Build complexity: NONE (binary install). [uncertain on exact minimum Ollama version that bundles a CUDA 12.8 runner, but 0.12.x+ confirmed; A6000 well within support]
gemma4_support: Yes — google/gemma-4-31B-it (dense 31B thinking model) is in the official Ollama library. Underlying format is GGUF (Ollama wraps llama.cpp). You do NOT manually supply unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF; you pull a ready tag: `ollama pull gemma4:31b` or `gemma4:31b-it-q4_K_M` (Q4_K_M), with `gemma4:31b-nvfp4` (NVFP4) and `gemma4:31b-coding-mtp-bf16` also published. You CAN still import a custom unsloth GGUF via a Modelfile (FROM ./gemma-4-31B-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf + ollama create), so unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF is compatible if you prefer the UD-Q4_K_XL quant — but the proper Gemma 4 chat template/parser must be attached for tool calling and thinking to work, which the library tags handle for you. Architectural gaps: Ollama's Gemma 4 template/tool parser has lagged upstream llama.cpp; several template/tokenizer fixes existed in llama.cpp (PR #21326 template, PR #21343 tokenizer) before being ported into Ollama, and a <unused25>/<unused49> token-spam bug was reported. Gemma 4 26B MoE has additional empty-response bugs not present on the dense 31B.
per_request_reasoning_toggle: PARTIALLY, and BROKEN on the OpenAI endpoint. Ollama has a first-class per-request `think` parameter on its NATIVE /api/chat endpoint: {"think": true|false} (also accepts "low"/"medium"/"high" for level-style models like gpt-oss). On /api/chat with think:false the reasoning phase is skipped and output goes straight to message.content, with any reasoning in message.thinking. HOWEVER, for Gemma 4 specifically: (a) on the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint the `think` parameter is SILENTLY IGNORED — Gemma 4 always thinks and content comes back empty (Issues #15288, #15293, #15368); (b) /v1/responses also ignores reasoning_effort:'none' (Issue #15635); (c) even on /api/chat, combining a system prompt + think:false + tools BREAKS tool-call parsing (Issue #15539). So a per-request hard OFF works only on the native /api/chat path AND only when you are not also using tools+system prompt. The exact field is `think` (native API). enable_thinking / chat_template_kwargs are not the Ollama interface.
per_request_reasoning_budget: NO true token-count cap. Ollama's `think` parameter is a toggle/level (true/false/low/medium/high), NOT a numeric token budget. There is no per-request equivalent of llama.cpp's thinking_budget_tokens=N or NVIDIA NIM's max_thinking_tokens in Ollama's API as of 0.20.x — you cannot say 'cap reasoning at 256 tokens.' For Gemma 4 the levels (low/medium/high) are not the documented native toggle behavior either; Gemma 4 thinking is governed by the <|think|> token the template injects, and you only get on/off, which is itself unreliable via /v1. This is a hard limitation vs. the project's need to cap reasoning tokens per request: the only way to bound reasoning on Ollama is to disable it (think:false on /api/chat) or accept full ~500-4000+ token thought blocks. [uncertain whether any newer 0.20.x build added a numeric budget; none found in sources]
tool_calling_support: Built-in but historically buggy for Gemma 4. Ollama implements Gemma 4 tool calling through its bundled llama.cpp engine + the Gemma 4 chat template, exposing OpenAI-style tools/tool_choice; there is no separate '--tool-call-parser gemma4' flag like vLLM. Multiple confirmed failure modes as of 2026: (1) parser crash 'gemma4 tool call parsing failed: invalid character' (#15241), partially fixed in 0.20.2 with regressions; (2) gemma4:e4b still showed tool-parsing errors after the 0.20.1 'fix' (#15315); (3) streaming via the /v1 OpenAI-compatible API drops tool_calls — the tool JSON is misrouted into the reasoning field with empty content so the client never sees the call (opencode #20995); (4) the specific combo system prompt + think:false + tools fails to extract tool_calls (raw JSON leaks into content, #15539, assigned but unfixed at filing). A community report flatly stated 'Ollama: tool parser still broken as of v0.20.1' when driving Claude Code. Workarounds: leave thinking ENABLED (tool calls then parse, but +10s latency and thinking-token leak), use the native /api/chat endpoint rather than /v1, and add explicit 'always use tools' system instructions. NOT production-reliable for an agent that needs OpenAI-style streaming tool calls.
openai_api_compatible: Partially, and notably broken for Gemma 4 streaming. Ollama exposes /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions with SSE streaming at http://localhost:11434/v1, generally usable with openai-python/httpx. BUT for Gemma 4 the OpenAI endpoint has serious deviations: message.content comes back EMPTY with all text placed in a non-standard 'reasoning' delta field (Issues #15288/#15293/#15368), which breaks any standard OpenAI SDK client (openai-python, LangChain, ai-sdk) that reads choices[0].message.content; the `think` parameter is ignored on /v1; streaming tool_calls are dropped (#20995). Teams have had to build a Node proxy translating /v1 requests to native /api/chat with think:false and re-emitting OpenAI SSE. So for a Python asyncio agent using openai-python against Gemma 4, the /v1 path is currently unreliable — you would need the native /api/chat client or a translation shim. The native API itself is solid; the OpenAI shim is the problem.
continuous_batching: Limited. Ollama processes requests with limited parallelism controlled by OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL (default small, e.g. 1-4) and OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS; it does NOT have vLLM-grade PagedAttention continuous batching. It inherits llama.cpp's parallel-slot batching. For the stated small scale (max 10 concurrent users, 4-8 parallel sub-agents) it can be made to work by raising OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL and ensuring enough KV-cache VRAM per slot, but throughput under genuine concurrency is weaker than vLLM/SGLang. For a single developer / light load it is fine; for sustained 8-10 concurrent agent streams it is the weakest option of the engines surveyed. [uncertain on exact default OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL in 0.20.x]
installation_steps:
Host-native, no Docker, Ubuntu/Debian RunPod pod on CUDA 12.8:
  # 1. Verify driver/CUDA (must show 570.x+ / CUDA 12.8):
  nvidia-smi
  # 2. Install Ollama (official script: installs to /usr/local, creates ollama user, enables systemd service on 127.0.0.1:11434):
  curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
  # 3. Confirm service:
  systemctl status ollama
  ollama --version
  # 4. Pull Gemma 4 31B (Q4):
  ollama pull gemma4:31b-it-q4_K_M
  # (Optional) import a specific unsloth quant via Modelfile:
  #   printf 'FROM ./gemma-4-31B-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf\n' > Modelfile
  #   ollama create gemma4-unsloth -f Modelfile
To customize (bind address, parallelism, context), edit /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/override.conf with Environment= lines (e.g. OLLAMA_HOST, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL, OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH), then systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart ollama. Pin a version from https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases if reproducibility matters.
serve_command:
Ollama runs as a persistent server (the systemd 'ollama serve'); you do not pass per-model serve flags like llama-server. Configure via environment, then pull the model:
  # /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/override.conf
  [Service]
  Environment="OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434"   # note: Ollama default port is 11434, NOT 8000
  Environment="OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384"
  Environment="OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4"
  Environment="OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1"        # keep model resident
  # then:
  systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart ollama
  ollama pull gemma4:31b-it-q4_K_M
To serve on port 8000 specifically set OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:8000. Reasoning is controlled PER REQUEST via the native API body {"think": false} (NOT a serve flag) — but note this is ignored on /v1 and breaks with tools+system prompt for Gemma 4 (see toggle field). Tool calling is enabled automatically when you pass `tools` in the request; no flag needed. There is no per-model context/quant flag at serve time — context is the OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH env or per-request `options.num_ctx`.
speculative_decoding: Not generally available for Gemma 4 yet. Google released official Gemma 4 MTP drafters (google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant, ~0.5 GB) on 2026-05-05 with claimed up to 2-3x speedup, listing Ollama among target ecosystems. However, Ollama support is still WIP: PR #15980 ('mlx: Gemma4 MTP speculative decoding') adds a Modelfile DRAFT command, --quantize-draft for ollama create, safetensors draft import, and speculation cache support — but it is under review, not released, and the initial PR targets the MLX (Apple) backend. As of mid-2026 you 'can run Gemma 4 in Ollama just fine but can't do the speculative-decoding part there yet'; MTP is 'mostly llama.cpp / vLLM / HF territory.' So mtp-gemma-4-31B-it draft + Ollama is not a working host-native CUDA path today. Expected speedup if/when landed: ~1.7-2x on code/predictable text, 6-8 draft tokens optimal for coding. [uncertain — PR status may change; CUDA backend support timeline unknown]
known_issues_gemma4: 1) /v1/chat/completions returns EMPTY content with all text in a non-standard 'reasoning' field for ALL Gemma 4 (26B MoE + 31B dense) — breaks openai-python/LangChain/ai-sdk clients (#15288, #15293, #15368). 2) `think` parameter (true/false) silently IGNORED on /v1 endpoints; only honored on native /api/chat (#15293, #15368). 3) /v1/responses ignores reasoning_effort:'none' (#15635). 4) Tool-call parser crash 'gemma4 tool call parsing failed: invalid character' (#15241), partially fixed 0.20.2 with regressions; gemma4:e4b still erroring after 0.20.1 (#15315). 5) Streaming tool_calls dropped via /v1 — tool JSON misrouted into reasoning field (opencode #20995). 6) system prompt + think:false + tools => tool_calls not extracted, raw JSON + stray <channel|>/token leaks into content (#15539, assigned, unfixed at filing in 0.20.6). 7) <unused25>/<unused49> token-spam tokenizer bug (fixed upstream in llama.cpp PRs #21343/#21326, ports lagged into Ollama). 8) Gemma 4 26B MoE returns completely empty responses on system prompts >~500 chars (#15428) — dense 31B unaffected. 9) reasoning_content re-sent in conversation history violating Gemma's contract -> context bloat (openclaw #68704). 10) Community: 'tool parser still broken as of v0.20.1' driving Claude Code. Net theme: reasoning-token waste AND tool-calling are both actively broken for Gemma 4 on the OpenAI-compatible path.
vram_usage: Comparable to llama.cpp since Ollama wraps it. gemma4:31b-it-q4_K_M weights ~18-19 GB (similar to unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL 18.8 GB), ~21 GB resident, plus a fixed ~3.6 GB Gemma 4 SWA KV cache and the regular KV for 16k context => roughly ~22-25 GB total at 16k on a single slot. On a 48 GB A6000 this leaves ~20+ GB headroom, comfortably enough to co-resident BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (0.13 GB) and BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 (2.3 GB). Higher OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL multiplies the non-SWA KV per slot, so size num_parallel against remaining VRAM. KV quantization is available but less directly exposed than in raw llama-server. [uncertain on exact resident figure for the specific Ollama 31B tag at 16k]
small_scale_fit: Mixed. Operationally Ollama is the SIMPLEST possible deployment (one install script, systemd service, `ollama pull`, host-native, no containers, trivial config, great portability to a future personal A6000) — operationally it beats llama.cpp on convenience. BUT the functional fit for THIS project is poor right now: the deployment is a developer-focused agent needing reliable OpenAI-style tool calling, per-request reasoning control, and a clean /v1 endpoint for openai-python — and all three are currently broken for Gemma 4 on Ollama (empty content on /v1, think ignored on /v1, tool_calls dropped/misparsed). For a casual single-user chatbot it's great; for an automated agent loop the bugs force ugly workarounds (native /api/chat client or a translation proxy). The low ops overhead does NOT justify the functional risk over the llama.cpp baseline, which gives you direct control of the same engine without Ollama's lagging OpenAI shim and reasoning-budget gap.
overall_recommendation: NOT_VIABLE (for this specific agent use case as of mid-2026), despite being the easiest to install. PROS: trivial host-native install on CUDA 12.8/A6000 (binary, systemd, no Docker), official Gemma 4 31B library tags, low maintenance, excellent portability to future personal hardware, can import custom unsloth GGUFs. CONS (decisive): (1) OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint returns EMPTY content for Gemma 4 with text dumped in a non-standard reasoning field — breaks openai-python directly (#15288/#15293/#15368); (2) per-request reasoning toggle `think` is IGNORED on /v1 and only works on the native /api/chat path; (3) NO per-request reasoning TOKEN-BUDGET cap exists at all (only on/off/level) — the project's core requirement to cap reasoning tokens cannot be met; (4) Gemma 4 tool calling is actively buggy (parser crashes, dropped streaming tool_calls, system-prompt+think:false+tools failure #15539); (5) no working CUDA MTP speculative decoding yet; (6) weaker concurrency than vLLM/SGLang. Bottom line: Ollama IS just a wrapper over llama.cpp, but it ADDS a buggy OpenAI shim and REMOVES the per-request thinking_budget_tokens control that llama.cpp gives you. For a developer agent you are strictly better off running llama.cpp (llama-server) directly. Reconsider Ollama only if the /v1 Gemma 4 content/think/tool bugs are fully fixed and a numeric reasoning budget is added.
